answer.rationale:
With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, any disruption from switching to an unproven-at-this-scale low-cost vendor (memory_c2) carries outsized delivery risk right at the moment the contract lapses in 14 days 
 an onboarding hiccup or invoicing mismatch would hit production with no slack. Memory_c4 shows the incumbent has previously ceded real price and term concessions under renewal pressure, and memory_c1/c6 show continuity with the incumbent has historically preserved delivery reliability and even unlocked further cost reductions via volume/term commitments. Given only one decision slot this cycle and a hard deadline, negotiating harder with the incumbent using the low-cost quote as leverage is the lowest-risk path to progress on the 18% mandate without introducing a new, unverified failure point in the supply chain. I want to verify the actual magnitude of savings achieved in memory_c4's original negotiation and the true onboarding/reliability details behind memory_c2's low-cost win before fully committing, since if incumbent concessions can't realistically approach 18% the calculus may shift toward add_second_source or a guarded switch next cycle.
